shlokas.sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच | धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः | मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ||1||
shlokas.meaning: King Dhritarashtra asked Sanjaya what his sons and the Pandavas, assembled in battle formation at Kurukshetra, were doing.
shlokas.guidance: Before making judgments, first seek clarity — understand the situation before reacting.

shlokas.sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच | दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकम् व्यूढम् दुर्योधनस्तदा | आचार्यमुपसंगम्य राजा वचनम् अभाषत् ||2||
shlokas.meaning: Sanjaya replied that when Duryodhana saw the Pandava army arranged for battle, he approached his teacher Dronacharya and spoke.
shlokas.guidance: When facing daunting challenges, we often turn to trusted mentors for perspective and guidance.

shlokas.sanskrit: पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम् | व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्या मैथिलीना ||3||
shlokas.meaning: Duryodhana described to his teacher the great army of the Pandavas, arranged in battle formation by Drupada’s son, who was his student.
shlokas.guidance: Acknowledging the strength and preparation of others helps us assess situations realistically.

shlokas.sanskrit: अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि | युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः ||4||
shlokas.meaning: He pointed out that there were many great warriors in the Pandava ranks equal to Bhima and Arjuna.
shlokas.guidance: Respect the capabilities of others; underestimating people can lead to poor strategy.

shlokas.sanskrit: धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् | पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः ||5||
shlokas.meaning: Duryodhana listed several valiant warriors on the Pandava side, including Dhrishtaketu, Cekitana, and the valiant king of Kasi.
shlokas.guidance: A clear inventory of strengths and resources helps in informed decision‑making.

shlokas.sanskrit: युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् | सौम्यश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् ||6||
shlokas.meaning: He also mentioned brave fighters like Yudhamanyu and Uttamauja, all of great valour.
shlokas.guidance: Valor is widespread; many capable allies may be overlooked if we focus only on a few names.

shlokas.sanskrit: अपर्याप्तं तदस्य ताक्ष्णं भीमसेन घोरम् | एवमुक्तस्य जग्राह मान्धाता दुर्योधनः ||7||
shlokas.meaning: Duryodhana said that this mighty force, however fearsome, was still not enough compared to his own strength led by Bhima.
shlokas.guidance: Pride and comparison can distort one’s view of reality and true capacity.

shlokas.sanskrit: पाश्यमकं पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम् | एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः उत्समाय च ||8||
shlokas.meaning: Observing the Pandava army, Arjuna spoke to Krishna when the battle was about to begin.
shlokas.guidance: Before acting, pause to reflect on values, relationships, and deeper purpose.

shlokas.sanskrit: अर्जुनम् उपसंगम्य राजा वचनम् अभाषत् | सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रम्यं चivité विमुक्तुम् ||9||
shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said that he did not wish to fight, standing between the armies, filled with compassion for friends and relatives on both sides.
shlokas.guidance: Compassion may cause hesitation when duty and love conflict; this calls for deeper self‑inquiry.

shlokas.sanskrit: सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विस्थितः प्रणब्धः पाण्डवः | शुश्रुमि न तु कौन्तेय धर्मस्य चानुशासनम् ||10||
shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said that he could not see anything but relatives and revered elders gathered for battle; he could not find any reason for war.
shlokas.guidance: When conflict arises among loved ones, it can cloud judgment and purpose.

shlokas.sanskrit: न जायते मम शरीरस्य का म्रत्युः किं वा बहुः ||11||
shlokas.meaning: Arjuna expressed despair, saying that slaying one’s own kinsmen in battle would offer no benefit, only sorrow.
shlokas.guidance: Questioning the cost of actions shows moral sensitivity, which is vital for right decision‑making.

shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said that no victory can justify killing those we respect and love, and nothing is worth it if it destroys dharma and duty.
shlokas.guidance: True wisdom considers the broader consequences of action before choosing a path.

shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said that deliberate killing of family and teachers would lead to sin and destruction of tradition.
shlokas.guidance: Be mindful of the long‑term moral and cultural repercussions of our choices.

shlokas.meaning: Arjuna stated that even if this war was fought for the sake of duty, killing those we respect in the name of righteousness would still be sorrowful.
shlokas.guidance: Righteous intention does not remove emotional and moral consequences.

shlokas.sanskrit: कथं न ज्ञेयः पितरो यस्मात्सर्वे तृणसहस्राणि ||15||
shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said that the souls of ancestors are countless and eternal, so how can killing their bodily forms ever reach the soul?
shlokas.guidance: Understand that life and death are aspects of a larger continuum.

shlokas.sanskrit: ऋषयोऽपि मृत्यो भवन्ति धात्रा च नासते समाः ||16||
shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said that even sages and fathers are mortal; therefore, killing their bodies does not destroy the essence of life.
shlokas.guidance: Material death does not equate to spiritual end; differentiating the level of existence brings clarity.

shlokas.meaning: Arjuna declared that without action, even inactivity is a kind of action; thus total inaction is not possible.
shlokas.guidance: In life, every choice or hesitation itself becomes a form of action with consequences.

shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said that lingering doubts and moral confusion robbed him of strength, and he did not know what he should do.
shlokas.guidance: When confused, seek clarity of purpose through reflection rather than impulse.

shlokas.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | मुक्तास्मि मे ह्येन्द्रियाणि येन्हि मनः संयम्यम् ||19||
shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said that his mind was confused about duty and he felt helpless as he lowered his bow and arrows.
shlokas.guidance: Admitting confusion is the first step toward gaining clarity and appropriate action.

shlokas.meaning: Arjuna declared that remaining inactive appeared better than killing his kinsmen for the sake of duty.
shlokas.guidance: When two goods or duties clash, resolve comes from deeper self‑understanding and spiritual insight.

shlokas.sanskrit: न जायते मम शरीरस्य का म्रत्युः किं वा बहुः ||21||
shlokas.meaning: He said if killing family is part of duty, then what benefit would victory bring if it meant destroying moral values?
shlokas.guidance: Victory without peace and righteousness is hollow.

shlokas.meaning: Arjuna’s sorrow grew as he questioned how one could kill parents and teachers simply in the name of duty.
shlokas.guidance: Respecting elders and ancestors shapes responsible leadership.

shlokas.sanskrit: नात्र संदेहः सन्ति येषां नात्र च श्रद्धा भवति ||23||
shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said that for those who have no faith or conviction, doubt and confusion lead to fear and despair.
shlokas.guidance: Develop steady conviction in values to avoid debilitating moral uncertainty.

shlokas.sanskrit: भोक्तुं यत्तु वा कर्तुं वा नाचमपेक्षते वीर्यवान् ||24||
shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said that one should not engage in conflict if the result is suffering, knowing that ignorance of duty causes harm.
shlokas.guidance: True courage discerns when to act and when to refrain.

shlokas.meaning: He said it is better to live in righteousness even if it means giving up life than to gain life by unrighteous means.
shlokas.guidance: Integrity holds more value than mere survival.

shlokas.meaning: Arjuna observed that no one can remain inactive even for a moment; every moment is filled with action.
shlokas.guidance: Life is constant motion; even in stillness, choices carry implications.

shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said that those who restrain themselves and are free from attachment neither grieve for the living nor for the dead.
shlokas.guidance: Detachment balanced with duty brings peace of mind.

shlokas.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | येशां चित्तं निरुद्धमावलि भूतानि ||28||
shlokas.meaning: Arjuna lamented that his mind was bewildered and he could not steady his senses.
shlokas.guidance: Inner turmoil can cloud judgment; cultivate inner calm.

shlokas.sanskrit: निश्चला तु मनो बुद्धिर्कृत्वा धर्म्ये स्थितो ययुः ||29||
shlokas.meaning: He said that those who stand firmly on righteous principles with steady mind and intellect achieve clarity.
shlokas.guidance: Steady focus on righteousness brings strength and clear perception.

shlokas.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | येहाऽहमहं मन्ये धनञ्जयः हरिश्रमः ||30||
shlokas.meaning: Arjuna wondered aloud whether it was better to kill his kinsmen and incur sin or to live in ignorance away from duty.
shlokas.guidance: Moral dilemmas arise from conflicting values; reflection is essential.

shlokas.sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच | एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप ||31||
shlokas.meaning: Sanjaya said that after speaking thus to Krishna, Arjuna cast aside his bow and sat down, overwhelmed with sorrow.
shlokas.guidance: Even the greatest warriors may feel despair when values are in conflict.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततः सञ्जय उवाच ||32|| न कोऽपि मध्येन राज्येन युद्धेन गौरवं वृद्धम् ||32||
shlokas.meaning: Sanjaya said there was no joy for a king or warrior in battle where relatives were fighting each other.
shlokas.guidance: War between kin yields no honor or lasting victory.

shlokas.sanskrit: एवं सत्यं युधि धर्मेण निगदितं हृषीकेशैः शास्त्रैः ||33||
shlokas.meaning: Sanjaya continued that what Arjuna felt was true to what wise scriptures declare — that anger and sorrow follow battles among loved ones.
shlokas.guidance: Scriptural wisdom supports the pain of moral conflict.

shlokas.meaning: Arjuna declared that remaining rooted in righteousness was of highest importance, even above life itself.
shlokas.guidance: Prioritize righteousness above all else.

shlokas.meaning: Sanjaya observed that Arjuna’s fear and sorrow left him weak and speechless, unable to act.
shlokas.guidance: Unresolved fear disrupts clarity of purpose and action.

shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said he saw his senses in turmoil, unable to focus on anything due to emotional conflict.
shlokas.guidance: Emotional overwhelm disrupts discernment; cultivate restraint.

shlokas.meaning: At this moment, Krishna prepares to respond to Arjuna’s lament with guidance.
shlokas.guidance: This marks the shift from confusion to guidance.

shlokas.meaning: Sanjaya related Arjuna’s words to Yudhishthira and others gathered, sharing his state of mind.
shlokas.guidance: Communication of inner conflicts fosters shared understanding.

shlokas.meaning: Yudhishthira expressed concern and support for Arjuna, seeking wise counsel.
shlokas.guidance: Supportive leadership strengthens resolve.

shlokas.meaning: He said that although Arjuna stood firmly, his heart was troubled by conflicting emotions.
shlokas.guidance: Outward composure can mask inner turmoil.

shlokas.meaning: Sanjaya continued describing the atmosphere of tension and uncertainty on the battlefield.
shlokas.guidance: In times of conflict, tension and doubt are palpable until clarity arises.

shlokas.meaning: Sanjaya reiterated the contrast of duty and suffering felt by Arjuna.
shlokas.guidance: Dualities of life — pleasure and pain — test decision‑making.

shlokas.meaning: Yudhishthira reiterated Arjuna’s moral dilemma, wondering what path was righteous.
shlokas.guidance: Leadership involves grappling with ethical dilemmas, not just strategy.

shlokas.meaning: Sanjaya described how Arjuna’s body and mind were affected by sorrow and compassion.
shlokas.guidance: Compassion can move even the strongest to pause and reflect.

shlokas.meaning: Sanjaya again stated that Arjuna’s mind was conflicted and his resolve was shaken.
shlokas.guidance: Conflicting values can destabilize resolve.

shlokas.meaning: Sanjaya emphasized that adherence to duty aligned with righteousness brings clarity and peace.
shlokas.guidance: Align actions with core principles to find peace in decisions.

shlokas.meaning: Sanjaya concluded by affirming that Krishna, the Supreme Guide, was ready to instruct Arjuna and dispel his doubts.
shlokas.guidance: Seek wisdom from those who embody clarity and compassion.
